//: The catalogue of Bloom release channels, read by .github/workflows/release-installer.yml.
This file is repo-wide and identical on every branch: it says what a channel IS, never
which branch publishes to it. That lives in each branch's copy of the workflow, as
CONTINUOUS_CHANNEL and the workflow_dispatch channel dropdown. Keeping this file the same
everywhere means merging between branches never changes anyone's channels.
A channel's range is the band of patch numbers its versions are drawn from. Each channel
restarts at the bottom of its own band for every new release line, which is what makes a
version legible at a glance: 6.4.108 is a Beta, 6.4.1281 an Alpha, 6.3.2 a stable release.
The workflow refuses to publish a version outside its channel's band, and refuses to
publish to a channel that is not listed here at all.
'Release' is the stable channel. Bloom.proj wants that one spelled as an empty string (it
is what produces Bloom.exe rather than BloomAlpha.exe, and the installers/ and deltas/
folders rather than installersAlpha/), and it ERRORS if handed the literal 'Release'. The
workflow does that translation at the msbuild boundary. Everywhere a person looks -- this
file, the dropdown, the logs, latest.Release.json -- the channel is called Release.
mustBeSigned says whether an unsigned build may go out on this channel. It is a property
of the channel and not of how the run was started: Beta and Release reach people who did
not choose to be guinea pigs, so an unsigned build there is refused rather than shipped.
The others would rather have a build than a gap, so a signing failure is reported and the
build goes out anyway. Every run signs what it can and reports what it got, whichever
channel it is for.
Adding a temporary channel: give it its own band. Bands from 4000 up are free;
temporary channels typically take 7000-7999 or 8000-8999. When one has served its
purpose its entry can stay here for reference, or be removed -- nothing depends on
it once nothing is publishing to it.
